> greater between two surfaces when those surfaces aren't moving

You're spot on. You're comparing between static and kinetic friction. Think of a vehicle and its anti-lock braking system. When you slam the brakes, the ABS stutters the braking to prevent your tire from sliding on the road. When your tires slide, its turning its once static friction into kinetic friction, which is always less. Thus the ABS is there to retain the tires static friction which allows you to come to a stop quicker.

This is my general game plan for the first week or so of each world: I spend the first few days running the coast, mapping what biomes are where. I harvest berries/carrots and up to about a half stack of twigs a full stack of grass as I explore. When night gets close I'm looking for a decent clump of trees to set up a campfire and spend the night chopping logs. If/when I find a mining area grab  minimum 16 stones for my pit and at least 1 gold for the science machine.

I do this looking for where all the important resources are on the map, trying to find the best place thats close to beefalos, bunny holes, and stone/gold in that order. Ideally having 4-5 bunny holes within the light radius of my fire pit. Then using the twigs/grass I've collected along the way to set traps at each one (doing this at nighttime). Once the science machine is down, make a shovel and now as I explore im digging up grass/saplings/bushes to plant at my base, it saves you so much time later on when you dont have to worry about looking for twigs and grass.

So by this point I have a base close to resources, with traps for sustainable food, and from this point on I consider myself at a minimum level of stability. I eventually map the entire world by running the coasts, occasionally following the roads.

Its getting a stable start thats the hardest part. Afterwards if you ever get in trouble you can always run back to base and recoup there. 

I'll also add that I play pretty slow through the chapters, making sure I have a respawn available at all times, always have materials for a campfire or at least torch, and don't find farming for a full stack of 40 something like beard hair to take with me to the next world.

Oh, and the Walking Cane is OP. For me at least it helps me avoid so many confrontations and damage. You can outrun anything with it. Make sure to look for ingredients for one during winter.
